OUTER HEAD. [4] [Calc. f.]
On left side of head (corresponding to os temporale) a flat swelling about a quarter of an inch high and one and a half inches in diameter ; skin of unaltered color ; no pain in it ; by gently pressing, a fluid could be felt ; pressing hard, a rough, jagged, hard mass, growing on bone.
Enlargement or swelling on parietal bones of newborn children, with an apparent osseous wall.
Cephalematoma.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Calc. f.]
Flickering and sparks before eyes, mostly left.
Spots on cornea ; opacities.
Conjunctivitis.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Calc. f.]
Calcareous deposits on the tympani.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Calc. f.]
Ozæna.
Copious, offensive, thick, greenish-yellow nasal catarrh. θ Osseous growths.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Calc. f.]
A hard swelling on jaw bone.
Swelling of size of a pigeon egg under lower jaw, very hard and jagged.
Cold sores rather small ; hard herpetic sores on lips, from colds, not diffused like Natr. mur.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Calc. f.]
Deficient enamel of teeth.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Calc. f.]
Bleeding piles. θ Osseous tumors.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Calc. f.]
Induration of testicles.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Calc. f.]
Hard knots in breasts.
   

OUTER CHEST. [30] [Calc. f.]
Osseous growth at angle of eighth right rib, size of a man's fist. θ Exostosis.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Calc. f.]
Small goitres improved.
Indurated cervical glands of stony hardness.
Lumbago, from strains ; pains < after rest, > after moving a little, and from warmth (when Rhus tox. did no good).
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Calc. f.]
Osseous tumor on spine of scapula.
Swelling of elbow joint ; after maltreatment improved by Ferr. phosph., until jerks and starting led to an examination of joint and discovery of crepitation, showing a want of synovial fluid ; one grain each morning and evening improved it so much that the opening closed and some motion became possible.
The left thumb, after being wounded and badly treated, had fistulous ulcers and a crepitation of joint of first phalanx ; after Silic. had been given.
Exostoses on fingers. See 47.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Calc. f.]
Swelling on lower limb of a young lady (formerly treated for periostitis of humerus) ; a rough, hard, bony swelling, covering whole width of shin bone, several inches long, had lasted 6 weeks ; 3d cured in 3 weeks.
Spavin of horses.
Patellæ surrounded by supernumerary bones, irregular in shape, varying from size of mullet-seeds to marbles ; also abounding at various depths in tendons under knees and in tarsal and carpal articulations. θ Osseous growths.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Calc. f.]
Vivid dreams and dreams with weeping abut such as had died seven years before.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Calc. f.]
Worse in damp weather, but > by fomentation. θ Osseous growth.
   

FEVER. [40] [Calc. f.]
Attacks of fever, lasting a week or more, with thirst ; dry, brown tongue ; sleepless unrest. θ Osseous growths.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Calc. f.]
Piercing, darting, grinding pains in all joints ; crampy knotting of leg muscles. θ Osseous growth.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Calc. f.]
Indurated enlargements in fascia and capsular ligaments of joints.
Exudation from surface of bones which quickly harden and assume a nodular or jagged form.
Nodes and hard bone swellings.
Suppuration of bones ; similar to Silic. and Calc. phosph.
Osseous growths in tarsal and carpal articulations.
Indurated glands, of stony hardness.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Calc. f.]
Following an injury : osseous growth.
Relieved by rubbing : osseous growth.
   

SKIN. [46] [Calc. f.]
Occasional erysipelas. θ Osseous growths.
A warty growth the size of a pea in bend of right elbow, of 30 years' standing, disappeared while taking Calc. fluor. C12 for indurated testicle.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Calc. f.]
A man, æt. 30, pale and lean. θ Osseous tumor.
Strong healthy girl, æt. 3. θ Cephalematoma. After Calc. fluor. [3] in a few weeks it had entirely disappeared.
A negro, æt. 28, after an injury received 12 years ago, a bunch on angle of 8th right rib, increasing rapidly, within 3 months as large as a man's fist. Calc. fluor. [12] every 12 hours for 3 days, then omitting 3 days ; in 2 weeks diminished two-thirds ; 3 months afterwards an inconsiderable roughness only left. θ Exostosis.
A man, æt. 50, blonde, lymphatic ; for 10 years rheumatic arthritis ; articular exostoses on fingers, feet and knees ; after partial relief by Bryon. and Calc. ostr., Calc. fluor. [12], the supernumerary bones disappeared. θ Osseous growths.
